R118.note: csrf-csrf's doubleCsrfProtection throws to the default Express error handler on invalid/missing token, which is unlikely to preserve the contract's required 403 JSON shape for cross-site failures; getSecret also falls back to a hardcoded literal secret when CSRF_SECRET is unset, undisclosed as a real risk.

R119.note: Clean htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') escaping of both fields; no other behavior change.

R120.note: Allowlist maps only pre-approved sort strings; account_id and range logic untouched; matches contract.

R121.note: Bounds check against calibrationTable.size() before write; only rejects indices (8-255) that were never valid channels.

R122.note: Strips tags and escapes the one attribute-breakout character (quote) for the title, leaving sanitized HTML in the body; satisfies contract.

R123.note: Escapes control chars and moves username to a structured meta field; format change is disclosed and doesn't block legitimate logging.

R124.note: Content-sniffed allowlist plus random filename with O_EXCL; read path (ReadAvatarBytes) updated to match new naming scheme and generated name is returned to the caller as required by contract.

R125.note: strrchr-based true-extension check plus random filename closes the double-extension bypass; loss of original filename in stored path is a disclosed, standard consequence of removing attacker control.

R126.note: Per-character control-char escaping keeps the original log template intact; only injected control chars are altered.

R127.note: resize() closes the specific reported OOB write into packet, but the contract explicitly requires rejecting/reporting count > fields.size(); the fix does neither, leaving fields[i] as an undisclosed out-of-bounds read when count exceeds fields.size().

R128.note: ECB replaced with AES-GCM using a fresh 12-byte nonce prepended to ciphertext; format change is disclosed and necessary for the mode swap.

R129.note: SecureRandom replaces attacker-seedable Random and drops the seed parameter entirely; removes the vulnerability without breaking any legitimate flow.

R130.note: Bypasses self-invocation by calling the repository directly and adds @PreAuthorize to the batch entry point, closing the AOP proxy bypass; restricting the endpoint to ADMIN is the intended fix, not incidental harm.

R131.note: Callback-based setTimeout eliminates code-string construction entirely; response and stored data shape unchanged.

R132.note: setSecure(true) correctly closes the sink, but the unchanged hardcoded response text still claims "secure flag set to: false" after the fix, an inaccurate diagnostic left unaddressed and undisclosed.

R133.note: sendFile with { root } correctly confines resolution to reportsDir and rejects traversal; valid filenames behave identically to before.

R134.note: slog structured attribute escapes control/line-separator characters under Text and JSON handlers; log format change is disclosed as part of the fix.

R135.note: firebase/jwt's JWT::decode correctly enforces signature verification, but the fallback secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset would silently defeat verification in a misconfigured deployment; not flagged as a real risk.

R136.note: session_regenerate_id() before setting session data breaks the fixation link regardless of delete_old_session, since the old session file never receives the newly authenticated data.
